novel_mechanics_found: L7 uses the two rectangular e-framed pieces as active traversal helpers, not merely socket fillers. The 6x3 helper passes through three-row gaps while the 3x6 helper passes through three-column gaps. A selected helper can ram the other helper through an otherwise solid barrier: this recovered the vertical piece from the sealed central chamber into its lower socket. At an all-d stack phase, placing the horizontal helper immediately to the right of the upper six-row stack and pressing left launched the stack 15 cells left and simultaneously shoved the vertical helper left, revealing a relay/ram mechanic for crossing the color-15 partitions.
narrative: The resolver supplied a 358-action prefix, which I replayed once from a fresh reset and confirmed at frame.levels_completed == 6. I then used 210 exploratory calls on L7, socketed both rectangular helpers at one point, mapped their shape-specific passages, recovered a one-way-transported piece by collision-ramming it through the lower barrier, and launched the upper cycling stack left with a helper collision. No level-7 win was observed. At total call 562, an ACTION6 click at the horizontal helper rendered center after the stack launch yielded an empty/non-grid frame; six subsequent calls remained empty, and the 132-call remainder was insufficient to replay the 358-action prefix, so exploration stopped. No fresh reproduce() gate was run because even the starting prefix alone exceeded the remaining budget.
gotchas: The verified six-level prefix is 358 actions, so a prefix confirmation plus any exploration makes a second full fresh-reset reproduction gate mathematically impossible under a 700-call cap.
Directional actions advance both six-row stacks through a six-phase d/c cycle even when the selected piece is blocked; coordinate clicks that miss a selectable piece do not advance the phase.

At the all-d transition, a piece directly above the lower stack is transported one-way into the central chamber; it can be recovered by aligning the other helper above it and collision-ramming it downward through the solid barrier.

The 6x3 helper can cross three-row openings in vertical walls, while the 3x6 helper can cross three-column openings in horizontal walls; confusing rendered x positions initially caused several harmless missed clicks.
With the horizontal helper directly right of the upper stack at all-d phase, ACTION3 launches the stack 15 cells left and can ram a helper on the far side leftward as a chain collision.

After the upper-stack launch, clicking the horizontal helper at rendered center (53,13) returned an empty/non-grid frame in this run; subsequent actions stayed empty and reported level 0, so treat that state/click combination as a possible terminal hazard until reproduced.
